title.narrative: Increased capacities of regional and sub regional constituents to effectively address the challenge of youth unemployment and under employment in Africa

description.narrative: The Regional Programme Outcome addresses the persistent mismatch between skills supply and labour market demand, which limits access to productive and decent employment, particularly for young women and men, including in the context of digital transformation and rapid economic change. The initiative contributes to the outcome of strengthened national capacity to design and implement inclusive and evidence-based skills development and youth employment policies. It supports more responsive and efficient systems for technical and vocational education and training (TVET), employment promotion and skills development. To achieve this outcome, the programme delivers the following outputs: Improved alignment of skills development systems and qualifications with labour market needs; strengthened monitoring and data systems for skills and employment, enabling evidence-based policymaking; operational youth employment action plans implemented in selected countries; improved capacity of national institutions and social partners to design and implement youth employment interventions, including in the digital economy; and strengthened knowledge base through research on the digitalization of labour-related services, including labour inspection, social security administration, employment services and skills systems, with a focus on access, inclusion, protection and labour market outcomes. The initiative primarily benefits young women and men, including those transitioning from education to work. It also strengthens the capacity of governments, employers? and workers? organizations, and training institutions. Implemented in collaboration with regional institutions, UN agencies and development partners, the programme promotes coordinated, youth-centred approaches to advancing decent work and inclusive growth.
